notes.claim: The first step in reading a fluid power diagram is to get an overall view of what is happening.
A schematic shows function rather than location, and each symbol shows a normal or neutral condition, so a new diagram is read for function and drawn state.
A one-line diagram is read from the incoming supply down to the loads.

sources.title: Engineering Symbology, Prints, and Drawings, Module 2: Engineering Fluid Diagrams and Prints (DOE-HDBK-1016/1-93)
sources.quote: Schematics are designed to supply the functional information of the system. They do not accurately represent the relative location of the components.

sources.title: Basic Diagrams and Systems | Engineering Library (US Navy NAVEDTRA 14105A, Fluid Power, chapter 12)
sources.quote: Each symbol is drawn to show the normal or neutral condition of each component unless multiple circuit diagrams are furnished showing various phases of circuit operation

sources.title: How to Read a Single Line Diagram | EECO
sources.quote: A one line typically starts at the top of the page and works its way down. It will start with the utility or other means of incoming power and its disconnecting device.
